# Psalm 89 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A contemplative poem of Ethan the Ezrahite. I will sing about the LORD's faithful love forever! Generation after generation, I will proclaim your reliability with my own mouth.

**2** I have declared that your faithful love stands firm forever — you established your reliability as solid as the heavens.

**3** God said: "I have made a covenant with my chosen one; I have made a solemn promise to David my servant:

**4** 'I will establish your dynasty forever and make your throne secure for every generation.'" Selah

**5** The heavens themselves celebrate your miracles, LORD! The angels praise your faithfulness!

**6** For who in all the sky can compare with the LORD? Which of the heavenly beings is anything like the LORD?

**7** God is deeply revered in the council of the holy ones — more awesome than all who surround him.

**8** LORD God of Angel Armies, who is as mighty as you? Your faithfulness surrounds you like armor.

**9** You control the raging sea; when its waves surge up, you calm them.

**10** You crushed the great sea monster like a corpse; with your powerful arm you scattered your enemies.

**11** The heavens are yours, and the earth is yours. You made the world and everything in it.

**12** You created north and south. Mount Tabor and Mount Hermon sing for joy at your name.

**13** Your arm is incredibly powerful! Your hand is strong, your right hand raised high.

**14** Your throne is built on the foundation of justice and righteousness; faithful love and truth walk ahead of you wherever you go.

**15** How blessed are the people who know how to worship you! LORD, they live in the light of your presence.

**16** They celebrate your name all day long; your righteousness lifts them high.

**17** You are their glorious strength; our power is lifted up because you are pleased with us.

**18** Our protector belongs to the LORD; our king belongs to the Holy One of Israel.

**19** Long ago you spoke in a vision to your faithful servant and said: 'I have given strength to a warrior; I have raised up a young man from among the people.

**20** I have found David, my servant. I have poured my holy oil on his head to anoint him.

**21** My hand will always be with him; my arm will make him strong.

**22** No enemy will get the upper hand on him; no wicked person will overpower him.

**23** I will crush his enemies in front of him and strike down everyone who hates him.

**24** My faithfulness and love will be with him; through my name his strength will be raised high.

**25** I will extend his rule over the sea and his authority over the rivers.

**26** He will call out to me: "You are my Father, my God, the rock who saves me!"

**27** I will also make him my firstborn son — the most exalted king on earth.

**28** I will maintain my faithful love for him forever; my covenant with him will never be broken.

**29** I will make his dynasty last forever — his throne will endure as long as the sky exists.

**30** But if his descendants abandon my instructions and refuse to live by my standards,

**31** if they break my rules and don't keep my commands,

**32** then I will punish their disobedience with a rod and their sins with a beating.

**33** But I will never take my faithful love away from him. I will not be unfaithful to my promise.

**34** I will not break my covenant or take back a single word I've spoken.

**35** I have sworn once and for all by my own holiness — and I will not lie to David:

**36** His dynasty will continue forever; his throne will last as long as the sun.

**37** It will be established forever like the moon — that faithful witness in the sky.'" Selah

**38** But you have thrown him aside and rejected him! You have raged against your anointed king!

**39** You've trashed the covenant you made with your servant. You've thrown his crown in the dirt.

**40** You've torn down all his walls; you've turned his fortresses into rubble.

**41** Everyone who passes by robs him; he's become a joke to his neighbors.

**42** You've made his enemies powerful; you've made all his foes celebrate.

**43** You've dulled the edge of his sword and refused to back him up in battle.

**44** You've ended his glory and smashed his throne to the ground.

**45** You've cut his reign short and buried him in shame. Selah

**46** How long, LORD? Will you hide forever? How long will your anger burn like fire?

**47** Remember how short life is! Did you create all of humanity for nothing?

**48** Who can live and never die? Who can escape the grip of the grave? Selah

**49** Lord, where is the love you used to show — the love you swore to David on your own faithfulness?

**50** Remember, Lord, how your servants are being humiliated! I'm carrying in my heart the mockery of all these nations —

**51** the insults your enemies hurl, LORD, the way they mock every step your anointed one takes.

**52** Praise the LORD forever! Amen and amen!

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **89:1-4**: This psalm starts with one of the most confident declarations in the Bible: 'I will sing about God's love forever!' The reader has no idea what's coming.

- **89:38-39**: The word 'but' in verse 38 is a theological earthquake. After 37 verses of magnificent covenant promises, the psalm pivots to: 'But you threw him away.' It's the most dramatic reversal in the Psalms.

- **89:46-49**: The ending of Book III has no resolution. The covenant seems broken. The king is humiliated. God seems to have lied. And the only response is: 'How long?' This is where Israel's faith was tested to the breaking point.

— PNEUMA
